Introduction The CDC Public Health Information Network (PHIN) is a national initiative aimed at enhancing the ability of public health systems to electronically utilize and exchange information. This is achieved by promoting the adoption of standards and defining both functional and technical requirements. PHIN Communication and Alerting (PCA) is a specific specification within PHIN that focuses on public health alerting capabilities, emphasizing the interoperability of systems used by various partners. Alerting, in this context, refers to the functionality required to manage time-sensitive public health event information, transmit it in real-time to relevant personnel and organizations, and ensure the delivery of this information is verified and monitored. Systems that provide PCA functionality must integrate these capabilities with the organization’s other public health information systems and processes while ensuring interoperability with partner systems. PCA is not synonymous with, nor a replacement for, the Health Alert Network (HAN). PCA is a technical specification for alerting, whereas HAN is a public health program that performs alerting. Most organizations with HAN systems are transitioning toward compliance with the PCA specification. Objectives The primary objective of the PHIN Partner Communication and Alerting Implementation Guide is to provide a detailed description of the functional aspects of public health alerting. To perform alerting in a PHIN-compliant manner, systems must process, send, and manage alerts in accordance with the requirements outlined in this guide. This guide defines the functional and technical specifications for systems supporting PHIN Communication and Alerting (PCA). It assumes the reader has a basic understanding of messaging and XML to effectively utilize the document. Audience This guide is intended for analysts seeking a deeper understanding of PHIN Communication and Alerting, as well as developers and implementers of PHIN-compliant alerting systems. Familiarity with this guide is essential for establishing PHIN compatibility. Document Structure The document includes the following major sections: Background and Problem Domain: Explains the underlying business problem of cross-jurisdictional alerting and the need for uniformity in public health alerting systems. Application Requirements: Defines the standard functional behaviors and technical standards necessary for public health alerting systems. PCA Alert Attributes: Specifies the set of alert attributes required for semantic compatibility across PCA alerting systems, including their vocabulary, semantics, and management. Vocabulary and Valid Value Sets: Details the vocabulary used within the PCA domain and the valid values for PCA alert attributes. PCA Cascade Alert Message Formats: Defines the formats for cascade alert messages and the mapping of PCA alert attributes to these formats. Appendices: Provides expanded examples of terminology, agency identifiers, and audience specifications. Standard attributes, attribute names, and vocabularies for PCA are defined and referenced throughout the document. Public health alerting systems are not required to use these standard names and vocabularies internally but must adopt them when conveying alerts across jurisdictional boundaries. Systems must be capable of translating internal information into the standard attributes and vocabularies to meet PCA requirements. Definition: Alert For the purposes of this document, an alert refers to a real-time, one-way communication sent by a PHIN partner organization to notify a collection of people and organizations about an event or situation of importance. Alerts may include both urgent and routine communications. A health alert is a specific type of alert that proactively addresses health events to mitigate their impact. Definition: Public Health Alerting System A public health alerting system refers to a system or collection of systems and processes used by a PHIN partner organization to compose, manage, and deliver alerts in compliance with PCA requirements. These systems must support various communication methods to meet functional and performance requirements appropriate to the event. PCA functionality may be implemented using a combination of information systems and manual processes. The term public health alerting system encompasses all systems and processes employed by a PHIN partner to implement PCA functionality. There is no requirement for a single system to perform all functions, nor for a PHIN partner to own or operate its own alerting system. Organizations may share systems, such as a city health department using a state-operated alerting system. The requirement is that PHIN partners have an alerting capability that meets PCA specifications. Uniformity in Partner Communications and Alerting A key objective of PHIN is to enable public health organizations to communicate and collaborate effectively, particularly during emergencies. Public health alerting systems must achieve a basic level of standardization in functionality, behavior, and terminology. Since many public health events are cross-jurisdictional, uniformity in alert message structure, vocabulary, semantics, and processes is critical to ensuring clarity and accuracy in communications. PCA aims to ensure consistency in the type of information sent, semantic compatibility with standard attributes and vocabularies, and alignment between alerting terminology, system behaviors, and human processes. Application Requirements A PHIN partner organization’s alerting system must be capable of creating, managing, and sending alerts to individuals and organizations involved in public health activities within its jurisdiction. Systems must operate 24/7/365 to send alerts to key personnel and organizations critical to the jurisdiction’s emergency response plan. Alerting systems must support both broadcast alerts to all recipients and targeted alerts to specific audiences as needed. They must accommodate various communication device types to ensure real-time communication, including during emergencies and after hours. Systems must allow recipients to confirm receipt and acknowledgment of alerts. The system must record and report each recipient’s acknowledgment and display delivery status information to the operator in near real-time. Secure Communication Alerting systems must provide secure communication for delivering alerts containing sensitive content. Secure communication ensures restricted information is accessible only to intended recipients. This involves restricting distribution, authenticating user identity, and using secure message transport methods. Alerts with sensitive content must be tagged as such and sent using secure communication methods. Alert Attributes and Vocabularies Standard attributes and vocabularies are essential for exchanging alerting information across jurisdictions. PHIN Communication and Alerting utilizes standard vocabularies and data structures defined by standards development organizations. Alert Format Standardizing alert formats ensures effective communication within and across jurisdictions, especially during emergencies. Each alert should address a single issue or health event. Alerting systems should render content appropriately for the recipient’s device. Alerts must include attributes such as a unique identifier, originating agency name, send time, severity, title, and message text. Sensitive alerts must indicate their sensitive nature to recipients.
